model:
The table shows how many international students were enrolled at universities in the USA, the UK, Australia, Canada and Germany in 2010 and 2022, together with the percentage change.
Overall, all five countries attracted more overseas students in 2022 than in 2010. The USA remained the leading destination throughout, but by far the most dramatic growth was recorded in Canada, which rose from last to third place.
In 2010, the USA hosted 723,000 international students, almost twice as many as the UK (405,000). Australia and Germany had broadly similar numbers, at 271,000 and 245,000 respectively, while Canada had the fewest, with only 130,000.
By 2022, the American figure had increased by 31% to 948,000. The UK and Australia saw considerably faster growth of 68% and 65%, reaching 679,000 and 446,000. However, the most striking change was in Canada, where student numbers more than quadrupled to 552,000, overtaking both Australia and Germany. Germany's growth of 50% left it with the smallest number of international students in 2022, at 368,000.
